"Rudradaman, a Shaka ruler, rebuilt the Sudarshana lake. Brahmanas advised kings to ensure that the varna norms were followed. Some groups, such as forest-dwellers and nomadic pastoralists, were outside the varna order and were often described as odd or uncivilised."
(i) Which ruler of the Satavahana dynasty claimed to be a unique Brahmana and destroyer of the pride of Kshatriyas? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'chandala' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Brahmanas tried to enforce the varna norms. (2)
items.answer: (i) Gotami-puta Siri-Satakani (ii) A category of people regarded as 'untouchable' by Brahmanas, assigned tasks such as handling corpses. (iii) They claimed the order was divinely ordained, advised kings to enforce it and persuaded people that status was based on birth.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Gotami-puta Siri-Satakani (ii) A category of people regarded as 'untouchable' by Brahmanas, assigned tasks such as handling corpses. (iii) They claimed the order was divinely ordained, advised kings to enforce it and persuaded people that status was based on birth.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Historians use the Mahabharata cautiously to study society.
items.answer: It was composed over a long period by different authors and was modified, so its content reflects many periods.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: It was composed over a long period by different authors and was modified, so its content reflects many periods. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about gender, property and social status is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "According to the Manusmriti, sons and daughters inherited the paternal estate equally."
items.answer: Sons inherited equally; daughters had no claim on the paternal estate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Sons inherited equally; daughters had no claim on the paternal estate.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about explaining social differences and handling the Mahabharata as a text is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The Buddhists accepted that social differences were divinely ordained."
items.answer: The Buddhists suggested inequality arose from human institutions and was not divine.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (The Buddhists suggested inequality arose from human institutions and was not divine.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.answer: In the Mahabharata, Gandhari advised her eldest son Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Stridhana could be inherited by her children without any claim by the husband. Sons inherited equally; daughters had no claim on the paternal estate. Men could acquire wealth in seven ways, women in six.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras laid down the ideal occupations of the four varnas. Brahmanas claimed that the varna order was of divine origin. Brahmanas were expected to study and teach the Vedas, perform sacrifices and give and receive gifts. Some groups, such as forest-dwellers and nomadic pastoralists, were outside the varna order and were often described as odd or uncivilised."
(i) Explain the term 'Purusha sukta', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Historians argue the varna ideal was not always followed in practice. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The varna order included chandalas as the fifth varna." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) A hymn of the Rigveda describing the origin of the four varnas from the body of the primeval man. (ii) Many non-Kshatriyas became rulers and many people pursued occupations outside their prescribed varna. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Chandalas were placed outside the varna order and regarded as 'untouchable'.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) A hymn of the Rigveda describing the origin of the four varnas from the body of the primeval man. (ii) Many non-Kshatriyas became rulers and many people pursued occupations outside their prescribed varna. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Chandalas were placed outside the varna order and regarded as 'untouchable'.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Marriage within a unit such as a kin group, caste or a group living in the same locality.
items.answer: endogamy
items.markingKey: (c) endogamy: marriage within a unit such as a kin group, caste or a group living in the same locality.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about gender, property and social status:
I. According to the Manusmriti, women could not claim a share of the paternal estate.
II. In the Mahabharata, Gandhari advised her eldest son Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas.
III. The husband had full control over his wife's stridhana.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: Stridhana could be inherited by her children without any claim by the husband.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the Mahabharata, kinship and marriage rules and answer the questions that follow.
"The critical edition showed that there were several regional variations in the Mahabharata. Under patriliny, sons could claim the resources of their fathers when the fathers died, including the throne. The critical edition project was based on manuscripts in different scripts from different parts of the country."
(i) Satavahana rulers were identified through: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'matriliny' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Mahabharata is a valuable source for studying kinship. (2)
items.answer: (i) metronymics, names derived from their mothers (ii) Tracing descent through the mother. (iii) Its central story is about a conflict between two groups of cousins, the Kauravas and Pandavas, over land and power.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) metronymics, names derived from their mothers (ii) Tracing descent through the mother. (iii) Its central story is about a conflict between two groups of cousins, the Kauravas and Pandavas, over land and power.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about explaining social differences and handling the Mahabharata as a text:
I. The Mahabharata was composed in a single year by one author.
II. The Buddhists accepted that social differences were divinely ordained.
III. The Sutta Pitaka suggests that people chose a king who would protect them in return for a share of their produce.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: III only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: It was composed over about a thousand years and by many people. II is incorrect: The Buddhists suggested inequality arose from human institutions and was not divine. III is correct.

items.stem: Explain the gotra rules prescribed by the Brahmanas and show how the Satavahanas did not always follow them.
items.answer: Each gotra named after a Vedic seer; members descended from him; women adopted husband's gotra and members of the same gotra could not marry. Satavahana queens kept names like Gotami and Vasistha from their fathers' gotras; some married within the same gotra (endogamy).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Each gotra named after a Vedic seer; members descended from him; women adopted husband's gotra and members of the same gotra could not marry. Satavahana queens kept names like Gotami and Vasistha from their fathers' gotras; some married within the same gotra (endogamy).
